The test image shows a close-up of a soybean leaf underside with:
- Extensive yellowing/chlorosis across the leaf
- A dark brown-black lesion with what appears to be a raised/pustular center
- Fine leaf hairs visible
- Polygonal vein pattern visible (suggesting underside view)

The dark pustular lesion on a yellowed background strongly suggests a fungal disease. Top candidates: Soybean_rust, Frogeye_leaf_spot, Cercospora, Bacterial_Pustule.

Let me view one reference from each top candidate.
Septoria brown spot shows yellow leaves with dark spots - a closer match! Let me continue checking more candidates.

Based on my analysis of all 16 reference images across 16 different classes:

**Test image key features:**
- Macro close-up of leaf underside (polygon vein network visible)
- Extensive yellowing/chlorosis of leaf tissue
- One prominent dark brown-black circular lesion with raised/bumpy center (likely pycnidia)
- Fine leaf trichomes visible

**Best visual match:** Septoria_brown_spot — references (Dise_107, Dise_12) showed exactly this combination: yellowed soybean leaves with dark brown-black spots, matching the background color and lesion character of the test image. No other class showed this specific yellow + dark spot pattern in close-up.

Other candidates ruled out:
- Cercospora: reddish-purple spots on green (not yellow) background
- Bacterial_Pustule: multiple small spots on green leaf
- Frogeye: circular gray-centered spots on green tissue
- Downy_mildew: powdery growth, not a discrete dark spot
- SDS: interveinal necrosis pattern, different appearance
